object_description: parallel volume slightly overlapping the existing hall, with a strict surrounding facade grid
design_condition: the new volume is aligned parallel to and slightly overlapping the existing hall, moved away from the plot boundaries so usable outdoor spaces are created around it

positive: Moving the building away from the boundaries creates usable outdoor spaces around it
This gives the necessary distance from the neighbourhood and a well-tolerated integration
The transition between private neighbouring environment and public use is successful
While based on the existing hall in setting, the volume stands out clearly in expression
The strict surrounding facade grid is distinctive
The spatial structure on the upper floor is clearly visible through the patios
Vehicle and pedestrian access are organised separately, which clarifies the situation
A large forecourt surrounded by a curved seating wall offers a high quality of stay
Its arena-like shape allows a wide variety of uses and events
The beach volleyball field and fitness area are directly accessible from the forecourt
The materialisation of the environment is well presented and consistent
Detailed statements are made about the design of the green areas
The selection of native trees, perennials and seeds is successful in design and ecological terms
The parking spaces all appear functional
Accessible and bicycle parking are well and centrally located at the main entrance
The entrance is exactly on the central axis and leads into a foyer
The structuralist organisation gives a very clear division into nine main rooms with patios
The play with spatial sequences is consistently developed with the offset heights
The proposed material meets the client requirements
The economic efficiency indicators are on average for all projects
The design is particularly impressive due to its spatial qualities for the art rooms
The idiosyncratic expression appears unexpected and courageous
negative: The new building is slightly higher than the existing hall
Playing fields and lounge areas along the border cause certain noise emissions
Direct visual references are only offered in the east-west direction
The ground floor use is not immediately apparent from outside
Abolishing the existing parking unreasonably worsens access to the existing hall
The corridors in front of the cloakrooms are too small for school operations
The connection to the existing hall leads through aisles that are too narrow
It is unsuitable for transporting larger sports equipment
The static system with storey-high wooden Vierendeel beams was assessed as unfeasible
The spatial play comes at the expense of flexibility
The operational organisation in the sports sector would have to be greatly optimised
The main deficiencies lie in the supporting structure and the final details presented
